text: So here it is, on the tissue you watched. In balance, division replaces lost cells. A mutation in a gene controlling division, perhaps from ultraviolet light, can disrupt that control, as in our example. Daughter cells inherit it, and divide repeatedly, building a <break time="0.1s" /> mass: a tumour. A benign tumour typically stays put; a malignant one invades, and its cells can spread in blood or lymph to form secondary tumours.
